submission.hypothesis: The locked Python graph grew from 9 to 34 packages because pyproject.toml pins `mcp==2.0.0` as a direct Host dependency for the `ordivon-host-mcp` server entrypoint (src/ordivon_host/mcp_server.py imports `mcp.server.MCPServer`, `mcp.server.transport_security`, and `mcp.types`), and the MCP SDK transitively drags in the full starlette/pydantic/httpx/etc. server stack. This is conflation of the Host CLI/Journal core (which needs only the stateless McpRuntimeClient for outbound Runtime MCP) with the inbound Host MCP server projection.
submission.causalMechanism: The package dependency surface conflates two distinct consumers: (1) the Host CLI/Journal/Doctor core that talks outbound to an Ordivon Runtime over MCP via `McpRuntimeClient` (a stateless HTTP client requiring only the MCP client/protocol surface), and (2) the inbound `ordivon-host-mcp` ASGI server (MCPServer + TransportSecuritySettings + pydantic models + starlette request handling for CallToolResult tools). pyproject.toml declares a single flat `mcp==2.0.0` dependency with no `[project.optional-dependencies]` split, so the locked graph necessarily resolves the full server+client MCP SDK tree for every Host install and for the deploy-frozen graph, expanding the lock from 9 to 34 packages. The Host semantic core and the 44/44 semantics pass depend only on the client/Journal surface; the expanded graph is driven by the MCP server projection carried by the Host distribution, not by Host semantics. No package split is justified from dependency count alone: the cause is the missing optional-dependency/entrypoint split between the client-only core and the server projection.
submission.nextFalsifier: Split `mcp==2.0.0` out of the unconditional `[project]` dependencies and install it only under a dedicated `[project.optional-dependencies]` entry (e.g. `server`) used exclusively by the `ordivon-host-mcp` console script, keeping the base `ordivon-host` CLI/Journal graph free of `mcp.server`/`starlette`/pydantic-server imports; then re-run `uv lock` offline and verify the base virtual environment resolves to the original 9-package frozen graph while the `server` extra reproduces the full 34-package graph, and verify `ordivon-host-mcp --check` plus the MCP-server test suite still pass when installed with the server extra while the base `ordivon-host` install lacks `mcpserver`. The falsifier fails (and the hypothesis stands) if removing the unconditional dependency leaves the base graph at 34 packages, or if the server entrypoint cannot import without pulling the server stack into the base lock.
